reviewerOutcomes.escalationCost: User: escalation is expensive and some issues cannot be solved without the user. Distinguish user-only issues from technical deadlocks before spending an escalation dispatch. Proposed zero-cost rule: orchestrator checks a short user-only checklist and stops/asks directly; escalation reserved for technical deadlocks. Categories: user-only = missing permission/credential, product/scope decision, external service/hosting, unclear requirement, destructive/irreversible choice; technical = plan contradiction, repeated test failure, interface mismatch, implementer/reviewer deadlock.
reviewerOutcomes.escalationRecommendsRewrite: User proposes escalator may recommend rewriting spec or plan on obvious logic bugs. Proposed: escalation output options include Fix with guidance / Rewrite plan / Rewrite spec / Split / Stop-Needs user; it must quote the bug and why implementation cannot satisfy it. Orchestrator presents recommendation to user; no automatic rewrite; after approval brainstormer/planner revises. Prompt-only.
reviewerOutcomes.approvalBoundary: User clarified: they approve the SPEC; the plan is for the machines, not for them to read/approve. Agents may revise/rewrite the plan freely as long as spec requirements, scope, acceptance criteria and security intent are unchanged. Any spec change requires explicit user consent. If implementation reveals the spec is wrong, stop and ask. Escalation mapping: Fix-with-guidance -> orchestrator proceeds; Rewrite plan -> planner proceeds; Rewrite spec / Split / Stop -> user decides. If a plan change would alter what is delivered or what is allowed, treat it as a spec change.
reviewerOutcomes.planReviewAndScopeCreep: User: every revised plan must pass the reviewer loop before implementation, checking it still delivers the spec and respects the spec boundaries. The reviewer must always look for silent scope creep: unrequested features, widened permissions, new dependencies, extra behavior, unrelated refactors, or changes that expand what the system may do. Silent scope creep in implementation = FAIL; in a plan = plan rejected and returned to planner, and if it requires a real scope change, it becomes a spec change requiring user approval.
reviewerOutcomes.whoRunsChecks: Current live policy allows routine local shell for all roles; role split is prompt-level. Implementer/gui-designer run build/test/lint/security and report exact output. Reviewer stays read-only and judges the diff plus implementer's recorded output; it does not rerun tests. Escalation may run diagnostic build/test/lint to reproduce a repeated technical failure, but no publishing/remote actions. Orchestrator does not run project checks; it coordinates and passes evidence.
reviewerOutcomes.explicitBlocking: User approved explicit blocking reporting. Implementer must report BLOCKED with the exact blocker, what it tried, and what it needs; no silent retry or workaround. Orchestrator routes by type: missing context -> supply; plan ambiguity/bug -> planner+reviewer loop; permission/credential/product decision -> stop and ask user; technical deadlock -> escalation.
reviewerOutcomes.escalationCapabilities: User approved: escalation gets full read of repo/docs/diff/review reports/registry/health and routing logs; may run build/test/lint and read-only git in the current tree to reproduce; may use a scratch copy when the problem is complex enough to justify the extra tokens; writes only an escalation report plus an optional unapplied proposed patch; no direct source edits, no publishing/remote writes, no permission changes.
